# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 75 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 75 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_075_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 75 presents the central image of Similitude 9: a great white rock with a gate, and a tower being built upon it. The gate is immediately identified as the Son of God (75:3) — the only entrance to God. This is an explicit christological statement, echoing John 10:9 ("I am the gate/door") and John 14:6 ("no one comes to the Father except through me").

The rock (*petra*) is ancient and cosmic — described as four-sided (*tetragonos*, "square/four-cornered") and large enough to hold the whole world (*dynasthai ton holon kosmon*). The gate is newly hewn, gleaming brighter than the sun. The contrast of ancient rock and newly cut gate encodes the theology that the eternal divine foundation receives a newly opened, radiant entrance through the Son's incarnation and exaltation.

The twelve virgins represent virtues — they will be identified later in Similitude 9. Their role is to carry and mediate stones from outside the gate to the builders inside. The gate is the christological threshold; only what passes through the Son enters the tower.

The six young men (*neaniskoi hex*) represent the six chief angels of creation who appear elsewhere in Hermas. They direct the building project.

The forty virgins (*parthenoi tessarakonta*) — not twelve — carry the stones. This expansion of twelve to forty may reflect the forty days of wilderness or some other symbolism, but SOPHIA notes the discrepancy between the "twelve" first mentioned in 75:2 and the "forty" in 75:5. This is in the source text; SOPHIA preserves both numbers.

The smoothness of the fitted stones is a perfection-symbol: redeemed souls fit seamlessly into the eternal structure.

---

## Similitude 9, Part 2 — The Rock, the Gate, and the Tower

**75:1** In the middle of the plain he showed me a great white rock rising up from the plain. The rock was higher than the mountains, square in shape, so that it could hold the whole world. This rock was ancient, and it had a gate cut into it; but the gate appeared to have been recently hewn, for it shone more brightly than the sun.

**75:2** Around the gate stood twelve virgins. The four who stood at the corners appeared more glorious than the others; but the others were also glorious. They stood at the four corners of the gate, two on each side; and additional virgins stood along the sides of the gate.

**75:3** And I said to him: "What is the meaning of the gate?" "It is the Son of God," he said to me. "There is no other entrance to God except through his Son."

**75:4** And I saw six young men come and take their place beside the gate, along with a great multitude of men who came to build the tower upon the rock. And the virgins who stood around the gate urged the men who came to hasten the building of the tower.

**75:5** The six young men who stood beside the gate directed the men building the tower to carry stones for the construction. And the forty virgins carried stones from the gate and handed them to the six young men, who received them and built.

**75:6** Those among the builders who were strong carried stones from the plain; others received stones from a certain rugged place and brought them for the construction. And the virgins carried them from the plain through the gate and delivered them to the builders for the tower.

**75:7** And when the bright stones cut from the plain were brought in, the men who had carried them trimmed and shaped them and handed them to the virgins, and the virgins carried them through the gate to the builders. And when the stones were set in the tower, they appeared exactly as they had when freshly cut — for they were so bright and gleaming that the joints were seamless.

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
